chapter_name: Biographies of Musicians and Scholars (Sangeetkar Aur Pracharyaon Ka Jeevan Parichay)
learning_objective: 👑 Draw inspiration from the lives and monumental contributions of Swami Haridas, Mian Tansen, Pt. V.D. Paluskar, and Pt. V.N. Bhatkhande!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: The great saint-musician of Vrindavan, a master of Dhrupad, and the guru of Tansen
The legendary court musician of Akbar who created numerous iconic Ragas
Founder of the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya; he elevated the social status of music and linked it with devotion and patriotism
The architect of the 10-Thaat system and creator of the most widely used modern musical notation system
The famous devotional song, beloved by Mahatma Gandhi, which was musically composed by Pt. Paluskar

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A 16th-century saint who lived in Nidhivan, Vrindavan. He was a master of the Dhrupad style. He refused to sing in royal courts, dedicating his music entirely to Lord Krishna. He was the esteemed guru of both Tansen and Baiju Bawra.

Born as Ramtanu Pandey near Gwalior. He learned music from Swami Haridas and Muhammad Ghaus. He moved from the court of King Ramchandra to Emperor Akbar's court, becoming one of his 'Nine Jewels'. He composed timeless Ragas like Mian Ki Todi and Darbari.

Born in 1872 in Maharashtra. He tragically lost his eyesight but pursued music fiercely. In 1901, he established the 'Gandharva Mahavidyalaya' in Lahore, the first public music school. He rescued music from disrepute, making it respectable for common families to learn.

Born in 1860 in Mumbai. A lawyer by profession, he traveled across India collecting rare compositions from secretive Gharana masters. He authored the 6-volume 'Kramik Pustak Malika', established the 10-Thaat system, and designed the notation system we use today.

The combined efforts of Pt. Paluskar and Pt. Bhatkhande transitioned Indian music from an oral, secretive tradition (Gharana system) to a structured, institutionalized academic subject accessible to all.

fun_activity.title: 🙏 Sing 'Raghupati Raghav'
fun_activity.instructions: Listen to Mahatma Gandhi's favorite bhajan, 'Raghupati Raghav Raja Ram'. It was Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar who famously set its widely recognized tune, composing it in Raga Mishra Kafi!

exam_tips: 📌 Who were the Gurus of Tansen? Answer: Swami Haridas and Sufi saint Muhammad Ghaus.
📌 A 5-mark question comparing the contributions of Pt. Bhatkhande and Pt. Paluskar (especially regarding their notation systems and institutional work) is extremely common.
📌 Who founded the 'Gandharva Mahavidyalaya', and where/when? Answer: Pt. V.D. Paluskar in Lahore, 1901.
quick_recap: ⭐ Pt. Bhatkhande often wrote under the pen name 'Chaturpandit'.
⭐ Pt. Paluskar sang 'Vande Mataram' at Indian National Congress sessions, deeply linking classical music with the Indian freedom struggle.
